About a year-and-a-half ago I applied for my first job. It was a chain grocery store that needed a lot of help at the time. Upon arriving to introduce myself to the manager I immediately decided that I wanted to work there because I was very attracted to one of the guys who was working at the time. It was the weirdest sort of attraction I've ever felt in my life. I don't believe in love at first sight. Mostly because I was inexperienced and never had a crush that lasted more than six months. Even when I did have crushes, I was never able to picture myself spending my life with them. It was almost as if I was self-aware about the fact that it was only an infatuation and wouldn't last, especially once I got to know them better.  But for some  reason when I saw this guy I had the strangest thought that I was going to be in love with him for the rest of my life. And here I am still gushing over him.  I ended up getting the job and was really excited to get to know him better. He turned out to be really nice and funny. I was so obvious that I'm pretty sure he figured out that I had a thing for him fairly early on. I put him so high on a pedestal that I was terrified of asking him out and ended up having a fling with another guy from that job. But the whole time I still longed for the man I knew that I was in love with (I'm gonna call him "Al" from now on). Especially since my summer fling ended up being an unbelievably abusive user. That was around the time I found out that Al was joining the military the next year. I was devastated.  That asshole ended up having to switch stores and after I recovered from the trauma and the store rumors about me started to die down, my friend that also worked at the store convinced me to confess to Al before he left. I did. He responded by telling me that he already knew and that he liked me as well, but because of the timing a relationship just wasn't in the cards. I took it as well as I could and we remained friendly.  We hung out more often and eventually built up a friend group made up of some of our coworkers. I was sad to know that Al was going to leave within a few months but I knew that it didn't  necessarily mean that I would never see or talk to him again. Thats what I would tell myself to make it feel better.   All of our friends easily picked up on the fact that I was madly in love with the guy. We all decided to go on a vacation together for a few days before he left.   That vacation was probably the happiest few days of my life.  We were always flirty at work but this vacation went wayyy beyond that. He acted really different. He would cuddle up close to me, comment on my breasts, and randomly kiss me when we were alone. We all had our own beds but he chose to sleep right next to me. It was so intoxicating and I felt like everything was falling into place, just like when everyone tells you that it eventually will.  On the last night of our vacation we ended up having sex. It was pretty much exclusively initiated by him. And it was both the best and worst thing that ever happened to me. I felt euphoric and knew at that moment that I was in too deep. The feeling of loneliness and temporariness crept up on me and I had a feeling that this could only end badly for me.  The next day he went right back to acting like a friend. And he stayed acting like that for the next few weeks until he left. He was really busy and the last thing that I wanted to do was bother him about taking a chance with a relationship. We threw a party for him for his last week with us but I ended up getting really drunk and crying the whole night. I couldn't even bring myself to really have a conversation with him. The next morning we said our goodbyes and that was that. I was so embarrassed about how I acted that I couldn't even bring myself to send him a text the day before he left.  My friends all noticed how dejected I was after that. They encouraged me to write him a letter or text him once he was out of boot camp. I kind of just wanted to let my feelings for him die at that point though. I had really had enough of trying to convince myself that he felt the same way.  Only I couldn't stop thinking about him. I dreamed about him literally every night and couldn't focus on anything but him on most days. After his time at boot camp had passed, I waited and waited for him to text me. I knew he wouldn't but I couldn't help myself. It developed into a really unpleasant pathological obsession.  A few weeks ago, one of my girlfriends finally convinced me to just check up on him.   I shot him a text and we had a pleasant little conversation before he had to go to sleep. I waited a couple days to see if he would initiate another conversation. Nothing.  I'm not stupid. I know what this all means. Sometimes I get a little angry because he did make me believe that he really liked me. But I also realize that I can't blame him for my feelings.  I want to be able to move on. I want to be able to not think about him every few minutes. I want to focus on my hobbies and my own betterment just as he is doing. But more than anything I still just want to be with him. I don't know how to fall out of love.

So, two years ago I was dating an amazing guy. He was really great, but for various reasons, the relationship didn't work out. I was very heartbroken at this time and ended up sleeping with a coworker of mine. This started technically a week before the end of my relationship with my boyfriend at the time... Yeah. I cheated on my first boyfriend. Great start huh?  Anyways, I obviously seriously regret this, it was the worst thing I have ever done. I hate myself for it. But I did end up dating the guy I was cheating on him with.  The best I can say of what was going through my mind at the time was that I knew my relationship with my parents was coming to a breaking point. Long story short, my parents are fairly conservative Christians. I am very much not that. I wanted to rebel in a big way against them and so I started doing risky and impulsive things I haven't ever really wanted to do. I tried ecstasy and shrooms even though I did not feel safe three out of the four times I did these drugs (twice did shrooms, twice ecstacy). I had horrible comedowns three out of four of the times; the day after doing drugs I usually felt like shit and once managed to get extremely depressed and cry into my boyfriend's shoulder that I just wanted to kill myself because I was so disgusting. Yeah. Pretty awful. Anyways, we broke up temporarily after that and GOD I wish it had've been a permanent break-up :(.   So we get back together and then I almost immediately head off to another state for a few months for work. We agree to do long distance and it goes pretty well for the four months I'm gone. But then I get home.  I visit my parents and they pretty much disown me after I come out to them as bi and confess I am dating an atheist. They did take me back into the family in March, but none of the issues were addressed and it always felt so tense. I started to lean more and more on my boyfriend. My anti-depressants weren't working anymore and every day was such a struggle. At one point, my housing became uncertain and I moved all my things into storage and moved in with him at his dad's house. I realize now, looking back on it, that I sort of forced him to let me stay. His response when I asked was "well... I'm not gonna say no." He said it so unenthusiastically and with a little scratch of his head that I now know meant "I don't want this." At the time I was thinking, "if he really loved me he would take me in happily" and I was so ecstatic that he said yes I couldn't even begin to imagine that he didn't want it as much as I did. Well, quarantine hit and it basically became him and me sitting around his house all day. Except I didn't feel comfortable. I tried to brush it off but I couldn't ignore the fact I was living in my boyfriend's elderly father's house. It was. So. Weird.  I decided to ignore the feeling (mistake) because I just *hated* being without my boyfriend. I *could not* be alone or I would get extremely suicidal. So my boyfriend became my lifeline. He was also pretty depressed and was despondent, thinking that he could never get better. Obviously, this led to a lot of both of us treating each other poorly and then resenting the other person. I always thought I had the moral high ground in every argument. I always thought I was right. He always turned every conversation into an argument. He hated being asked to change. He mostly just wanted a pretty thing to have sex with that could also be his therapist. I was looking for someone to take me in and care for me to replace the love my parents couldn't show me and who could also have sex with me. So. This was obviously a great and healthy turn in the relationship. We had a lot of sex and smoked a lot of weed, he got a cat, and I kept living there for almost TWO MONTHS. To be fair, my housing situation was a bit uncertain and I was supposed to have a roommate which I knew would help my not-being-able-to-be-alone situation. Well, she backed out right before we signed the lease and I had to find somewhere else to live. I eventually did find a place but delayed really moving in because I still didn't want to be alone.  Y'all, I literally lived in this boy's home with his father there for nearly TWO MONTHS. I basically pushed him to do this and even though I didn't realize I was doing it at the time, that still doesn't excuse my actions. Even more, though, is that after we broke up, I spent a long time trash-talking him to my friends. Some of them even knew him. He was not the nicest of people though and they were not friends of his to begin with. I made it seem like I was innocent and did nothing wrong and he was an evil villain who ruined everything and traumatized me.   In reality, I was just as shitty as he was. Maybe even shittier, honestly. All I can say for myself is that once we broke up, I took my time to grieve and ended up realizing a lot of things about myself. I  learned that I can be impulsive, reckless, and emotional and I dealt with that by being controlling. I was manipulative and basically using him to replace my broken family. Neither of us were in love with the other anymore. This relationship made both of our lives worse. He realized it before I did, but I am grateful that we broke up. We weren't good for each other and we had so much work to do on ourselves.  I'm glad to say that I've turned my life completely around. I am currently in a healthy relationship with a wonderful man and I have mended many fences with friends. I have been going to therapy regularly and the dose on my meds has been increased. I am a healthier person with healthier relationships. I still don't know how I can forgive myself for all of this, but all I can do is move forward and try to be a better person.

It's difficult to describe but if you see and feel sadness in most things in life you could have dysthymia. Constant, uncontrollable crying, thinking often about sad topics. A proper diagnosis is needed. This illness generally develops prior to adulthood and can be described as a constant low mood depression. You can google "dysthymia mood disorder" to receive a full description. The disorder makes one feel alone, desperate and unusual. I have a friend I went to school with, he never cried in 35 years I knew him until his father died. He was uncontrollable that funeral day. The next day we chatted. I mentioned that his state the day before was how I felt every second day. He got some idea of the magnitude. Soon after I got the diagnosis Bipolar2, depression, anxiety and...dysthymia. my psychiatrist discovered that a near drowning of my brother when I was 12yo was the spark, the shock that set it off. I didnt talk for 3 months after that incident and was highly emotional ever since until 2009 when he prescribed medication. Since then my life has turned around in terms of sadness. If you believe your level of sadness is high, constant and you feel desperate, even suicidal, you might have dysthymia. It effects more women than men, can come about if you have a parent with a mental illness or if you suffered trauma at a young age. Seek help. The difference to your life will be much more positive.
